independent_question: How does observed seasonal overlap between frog calling records and stage-labelled adult odonate sightings vary over years and latitude within Australia, and when is this observable opportunity inconsistent with trophic-switch/alarm inference?

source_streams.label: FrogID_positive_species_occurrence
source_streams.note: All documented frog calls; species occurrence rows not distinct recordings and not submitted negatives

source_streams.label: Odonata_stage_Adult
source_streams.note: Verified explicitly tagged adult odonates, a subset of all records

source_streams.label: Odonata_all_life_stage_states
source_streams.note: Sensitivity for the missingness/annotation bias of Adult label

source_api: https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search?limit=0&facet=month&facetLimit=12; use country=AU for Odonata, datasetKey for FrogID, year and lat band
normalization: p_{g,b,y,m}=n_{g,b,y,m}/sum_m n_{g,b,y,m} for g group. This is within-source seasonal observation composition, not an absolute ecological probability.
secondary_stats: circular mean month and circular concentration R
rotational alignment relative to all 12 integer monthly rotations of one vector
significance_policy: Original source exploratory; no confirmatory stage reversal or acoustic warning; do not pool 36 correlated cell-year units as independent populations.
max_claim: source observation-level seasonal phase/overlap heterogeneity across Australia; possible ecological timing hypothesis only
missingness_contraints: Do not replace unknown lifeStage with adult; all odonate records sensitivity only. No co-location to specific wetland. E.g. early source feasibility shows AU Odonata 147911 total (2018–24), Adult 19999, nymph105, Larva3; AU Anura 1378754 total, Larva88, Egg20. Species-specific lifeStage data extremely thin.
preregistered: The six band×six year analysis grid and thresholds are defined before all 36 original readouts; a small 2019 south and 2020 north feasibility pilot was previously read.
